aging-cells.def: The build-up of DNA damage, damaged proteins and failing mitochondria in cells, with shortening telomeres (the capped repeat sequences at chromosome ends) and senescence, a permanent stop to division in a cell that stays alive and releases inflammatory signals.

aging-systems.def: The changes in each organ system with age: working units such as nephrons, motor units, elastic fibers and naive T cells are lost, so resting function is usually kept but reserve, the extra capacity available under stress, shrinks.
